question: With its decree of September 2023 (‘Decreto Sud’), the Italian Government enacted new rules for immigration removal centres (IRCs) ‘intended for defence and national security’. The changes legally equated IRCs with military bases and structurally with maximum security prisons. Under the new rules, it will be impossible to know what happens inside these facilities.

Moreover, the maximum detention time for migrants in the new IRCs has been lengthened to 18 months. Even before the new law was passed, several non-governmental organisations had reported violations of migrants’ rights in the IRCs and poor living conditions for the people detained there. With the new law, migrants’ rights will be totally swept away. 1.
Does the Commission consider that the detention of migrants in military prisons respects human rights, as outlined in the Treaties?
Will the Commission ask Italy for clarification on this matter?
